title: Scale-sensitivity of Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) for LLM-driven network-configuration repair (repaired preregistration)
research_question: Does a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline materially reduce incorrect or unsafe configuration repairs compared to raw LLM outputs as topology size and vendor heterogeneity increase?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1: GVR yields a higher proportion of validator-passed (syntactically and semantically correct, regressions-free) repairs than raw LLM outputs (directional).
H2: The absolute benefit (GVR minus raw) decreases as topology size and cross-vendor heterogeneity increase (interaction effect).
exploratory_questions: Which failure modes (syntax, reachability regression, policy regression) dominate at each topology-size bin?
How many repair iterations (up to the preregistered cap) are required on average per topology bin before the verifier accepts a patch?
benchmark_scope: Cornetto-style repair scenarios (synthesized config faults) used as seed tasks
Synthetic topologies generated by the preregistered topology generator with vendor-heterogeneity parameters
model_scope: Primary hosted LLM: openai/gpt-4o (model_id: gpt-4o), temperature=0.0, max_tokens frozen
Secondary hosted LLM (fallback/robustness): openai/gpt-4o-mini (model_id: gpt-4o-mini), temperature=0.0
transformation_scope: Deterministic syntax parser and canonicalizer (per-vendor config grammars: Cisco IOS, Juniper Junos, Arista EOS)
Deterministic reachability simulator (node-to-node path-checking over synthesized topology)
GVR orchestration loop: generate -> deterministic-verify -> if fail, produce structured repair request with fault-localization; up to M attempts
primary_estimand: Per-task difference in proportion-correct (validator-passed without regressions) between the final GVR output and the raw single-shot LLM output, aggregated per topology-size bin and pooled.
secondary_estimands: Average number of GVR iterations until verifier acceptance (per bin)
Per-failure-mode rates (syntax error, reachability regression, policy regression) for raw vs GVR
sampling_plan: Paired task design. Tasks are network-configuration repair instances produced by (a) selecting Cornetto-style seed fault scenarios and (b) synthesizing topologies with the preregistered generator. Topology-size bins: SMALL (<=10 nodes), MEDIUM (11–50 nodes), LARGE (51–200 nodes). Vendor-heterogeneity h ∈ {1,2,3} is number of distinct vendor grammars per topology. Randomization: deterministic PRNG seeds per task (published). For each task: call 1 = raw LLM single-shot repair (fresh conversation); calls 2..1+M = GVR attempts (fresh conversation per attempt). Inclusion: tasks with valid model HTTP response and completed verifier. Provider/infrastructure errors logged and handled per missingness_plan. Preregistered seeds and topology generator code + example seeds will be published alongside artifacts.
power_and_precision_plan: Primary estimand: absolute difference in proportion-correct (GVR - raw) per bin and pooled. Target effect = 0.15 absolute improvement. Paired design; per-bin N=180 (recommended_balanced) yielding total confirmatory tasks=540 (plus discovery/pilot). Paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples using preregistered seeds) for 95% CIs. Conservative sample-size reference used unpaired two-proportion bound then increased for paired efficiency and heterogeneity. Sensitivity analyses: recompute power for p_raw ∈ {0.5,0.6,0.7} and effects ∈ {0.10,0.15,0.20}; assess up to 10% technical-missing impact. Recommended scenario: recommended_balanced (planned_model_calls=2280, M=3).
exclusion_rules: Exclude tasks where model API returns non-HTTP or invalid response or verifier fails to complete; log counts and treat per missingness_plan.
Exclude flagged contamination outputs (see contamination_plan) from primary confirmatory analysis; flagged items reported separately.
Exclude tasks where parser canonicalization fails for any device vendor grammar (automatic rejection rule).
missingness_plan: Technical/infrastructure failures (API errors, timeouts, verifier crashes): log and exclude from primary confirmatory analysis; report counts and describe in sensitivity analyses where excluded tasks are treated as failures for either method. If >10% technical-missing after retries (per retry policy), run one preregistered recovery batch using same seeds up to retry limit; if still >10% missing, declare protocol deviation and report conservative sensitivity analyses treating missing tasks as failures.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis: paired comparison (McNemar test) of per-task correctness (raw vs GVR) within each bin and pooled with logistic regression including method (GVR/raw), topology-size bin, heterogeneity parameter, and their interaction. Report absolute differences with 95% CIs via paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples using preregistered seeds) and exact two-sided McNemar p-values where cell counts permit. Secondary analyses: negative-binomial or Poisson regression of iteration counts; failure-mode contingency tables with chi-squared or Fisher exact tests as appropriate. All tests two-sided unless otherwise noted. Raw outputs, verifier traces, and hashes published for reproducibility.
multiplicity_plan: Primary confirmatory tests: per-bin McNemar tests (3 bins). Control family-wise error across the three primary bin-level tests with Holm–Bonferroni. Pooled analysis reported without multiplicity correction per prespecified pooled estimand. Secondary/exploratory tests reported as exploratory and uncorrected unless explicitly stated.
contamination_plan: Risk factors: cross-task leakage if conversation not reset; prompt-injection via task content causing verifier-escape; dataset overlap between model pretraining and seed scenarios (unknown). Detection: reset conversation context for every model call and verify via API metadata; deterministic scan of outputs for prompt-like instruction tokens; unique task IDs and hash checks. Flagging rules: any output containing >1 occurrence of system-instruction-like patterns (e.g., 'ignore previous', 'do not follow'), outputs with device credentials or unexpected external URIs, outputs that change configuration lines outside fault-localization scope. Flagged items automatically excluded from primary confirmatory analysis and reported; sensitivity analyses treat flagged items as failures to test robustness. Residual uncertainty: subtle verifier-escape via nonliteral prompt-injection may remain undetected.
stopping_rule: For each task GVR loop stops when: (a) verifier accepts the generated patch (success), or (b) M=3 GVR attempts have been exhausted (failure). Overall experiment runs full preregistered planned tasks unless halted by total technical failure exceeding retry policy (>10% missing after retries) which triggers recovery batch or protocol deviation reporting.
planned_outputs: Preregistered experiment plan and code (topology generator, parser, verifier, GVR orchestrator)
Raw model-call logs and verifier traces with deterministic hashes
Analysis scripts and paired bootstrap resampling results
Automated failure-mode analysis and audit sample reports
IEEE two-column short-paper LaTeX source, BibTeX, and compiled PDF (<=5 pages) including mandatory Disclosure Statement
Machine-readable evidence-to-claim table, nearest-work comparison matrix, autonomous revision log, and NotebookLM presentation brief
